review_evidence: The complete unit contains 163 primary Lean files spanning the Soma parser, elaborator/typechecker, compiler lowering, LLVM/codegen, build driver, LSP and compiler tests; the README describes a dependently typed functional language compiling to native code via LLVM.

An exhaustive theorem/lemma/example/axiom scan across all 163 primary Lean files found proposition declarations in exactly two files: 15 elementary algebra/order facts for the three-element QTT Quantity datatype and one freshness fact for compiler-generated unique IDs.

No formal semantics, soundness, type-safety, compiler-correctness, refinement, or standalone mathematical development is present; the remaining declarations implement the compiler/runtime/tooling itself.

source_action.content_invariant: All 163 primary Lean files were inventoried and the complete proposition-declaration surface was enumerated. The only theorem-bearing files are Core/Quantity.lean (15 finite-case algebra/order facts about the compiler's usage-count datatype) and Unique.lean (one fresh-ID inequality); all other source is parser/elaborator/compiler/build/LSP/test implementation. Retirement therefore removes a large application-programming vocabulary without hiding a formal semantics or verification corpus.
evidence: README: Soma is a dependently typed pure functional language compiler targeting native code via LLVM and interaction-net/QTT compilation.
Complete theorem/lemma/example/axiom scan: proposition declarations occur only in compiler/Lib/Soma/Core/Quantity.lean and compiler/Lib/Soma/Unique.lean.

Quantity.lean was inspected in full: its 15 theorems are case-split identity/commutativity/associativity/distributivity/order facts for {0,1,omega}; Unique.lean's sole theorem proves two sequentially generated numeric IDs differ.
source_action.rationale: Soma is an executable compiler/language/LSP implementation. Its few checked propositions are local implementation invariants, not an independently addressable mathematical or formal-methods development suitable for prior-art search.

summary: Reviewed Soma and retire it as a compiler/language implementation whose proposition-bearing surface is limited to local implementation invariants rather than an independent formalization/specification proof corpus.
